summary: Explore Kurdistan's rock layers, geological formations and stratigraphic sections.
description: Kurdistan's geological history is recorded in successive rock layers. This collection brings together documented formations and stratigraphic sections, with descriptions of their lithology, thickness, boundaries and age evidence where available. The profile photograph shows exposed rock in Rawandiz Canyon; it does not identify a formation or assign an age to the outcrop. Image: Rawandiz Canyon (Kharand) 03 — Khoshhat. CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0). Resized for display. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Rawandiz_Canyon_(Kharand)_03.jpg

summary: Explore fossil evidence and the history of life recorded in Kurdistan's rocks.
description: This collection documents body fossils, microfossils and trace fossils associated with geological research in Kurdistan. Records distinguish observed features from interpretations and link identifications, ages and localities to supporting evidence. The profile photograph shows a fossil displayed at the Erbil Stones and Gems Museum. Its original locality and geological age are not established by the photograph. Image: Fossil. From? Period? summary: Discover Kurdistan's rocks and minerals through documented specimens and outcrops.
description: Explore the materials that make up Kurdistan's geological landscape, from sedimentary rocks to igneous and metamorphic rocks and mineral specimens. Records describe observable textures, composition and geological context, with identifications supported by evidence where available. The profile image shows agate labelled as originating from Kurdistan, Iraq, on display at the Erbil Stones and Gems Museum. Image: Agate from Kurdistan, Iraq (the so-called Peshmerga agate). summary: Explore folds, faults and fractures that shape Kurdistan's geological structure.
description: Kurdistan lies within the wider Zagros mountain system, where geological structures record deformation of the crust. This collection brings together documented folds, faults, shear zones, joints and fractures, including measurements and interpretations where supported by evidence. The profile image is a regional map of the Zagros Folded Zone, providing context rather than a site-specific geological survey. Image: Zagros Folded Zone — Joshua Doubek. CC BY-SA 3.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0). Resized for display. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Zagros_Folded_Zone.jpg

summary: Explore groundwater, springs, wells and aquifers across Kurdistan.
description: Hydrogeology examines how water is stored and moves through rock and sediment. This collection brings together documented springs, wells and aquifers in Kurdistan, with information on geological setting, flow and water characteristics where measured. The profile photograph shows Bekhal Spring and waterfall in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq; water quality and aquifer properties require separate evidence. Image: Bekhal Spring 01 — Khoshhat. CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0). Resized for display. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Bekhal_Spring_01.jpg

summary: Explore Kurdistan's landforms and the deposits and processes shaping its surface.
description: Kurdistan's surface landscape includes incised valleys, rocky slopes, caves and younger sediment deposits. This collection documents Quaternary and other surficial deposits alongside karst and erosional landforms, linking descriptions and interpretations to field observations or published evidence. The profile photograph shows Rawandiz Canyon in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq. Image: Rawandiz Canyon (Kharand) 01 — Khoshhat. CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0). Resized for display. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Rawandiz_Canyon_(Kharand)_01.jpg
